issues.title: screenshot positional argument misinterpreted as CSS selector instead of filename

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 screenshot ".test-sessions/my-file.png"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Screenshot saved to .test-sessions/my-file.png, or an error message that the path is not a valid CSS selector.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Screenshot saved to default .browser4-cli/snapshot/screenshot-<timestamp>.png with no error or warning about the ignored argument. The 3-byte file suggests a broken capture.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The positional argument to `screenshot` is defined as `[ref]` (CSS selector or snapshot ref), not a filename. The `--filename`/`-o` flag must be used for custom paths. The CLI silently treats an invalid path as an unresolved CSS selector and falls back to a full-page screenshot saved at the default location, without warning the user.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands/screenshot.rs: argument parsing and resolution logic

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- When the positional argument contains a path separator (/ or \) and does not look like a CSS selector, warn the user that they probably meant --filename
- Consider a heuristic: if the arg ends in .png/.jpg/.jpeg and doesn't start with #/./[a-zA-Z], suggest --filename
- Add a tip to screenshot help: "To specify a filename, use --filename or -o; the positional argument is a CSS selector."

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect auto-discovers wrong container pattern when no selector given

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: On a product detail page, run `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot inspect --max 3 --depth 2` without specifying a selector.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The tool should inspect the main content area (#product-page) or prompt the user to specify a starting selector when multiple repeating patterns exist.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The tool auto-discovered `.recommendation-card` elements (the 'Customers also viewed' section at the page bottom) instead of the product detail content. The product's title, price, description, and image selectors were not surfaced.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Inspect's auto-discovery walks from `:root` looking for sibling-group repeating patterns. The recommendation cards (4 siblings) are more structurally regular than the single product detail container, so they're picked first. The user has no way to direct discovery toward the main content without already knowing the right container selector.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/... (htmlsnapshot inspect logic — auto-discovery heuristic from :root)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- When multiple sibling-group patterns exist, list them all with a summary line so the user can pick one with `inspect <selector>`
- Prioritize patterns with larger bounding boxes (main content area) over smaller ones (sidebars, recommendations)
- Add a hint after auto-discovery: "To inspect the main product area, try: htmlsnapshot inspect '#product-page'"
- Document in SKILL.md that `htmlsnapshot inspect` with no selector auto-discovers from :root and may pick sidebars

issues.title: htmlsnapshot get all text with class-based selectors fails silently on product description

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all text "#product-page [class*='about']" on the product detail page after htmlsnapshot capture.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Returns text content from elements matching the attribute selector.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Returns empty array with message: "No elements matched. The snapshot may be stale..." even though the selector was based on observed class names in the page. Multiple attempts with different class patterns ([class*='about'], .about-section, [class*='section']) all returned empty.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Likely a mismatch between the CSS class names rendered in the stored HTML snapshot and the class patterns being tried. The htmlsnapshot captures initial server HTML, but the class names may not match expected patterns. Alternatively, the attribute selector syntax may have limited support in the htmlsnapshot CSS engine.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/... htmlsnapshot CSS selector engine (class attribute matching)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- When no elements match, suggest using `htmlsnapshot inspect` with a broader selector to discover actual class names
- Consider adding a `--suggest` flag that prints the top-N class names found in the snapshot when a selector returns empty
- Document common class name patterns for MockSite product pages in the scenario description

issues.title: Interactive-only snapshot (-i) output is excessively verbose due to parent text accumulation

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 snapshot -i --stdout on a content-rich e-commerce page.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Interactive-only snapshot should show clearly delineated interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs) with concise labels.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Parent elements accumulate all descendant text into their accessible names. For example, a product card `article` element shows its entire text content concatenated (title + price + rating + description + badge), making it hard to distinguish interactive children from noise.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The AX tree's accessible name computation for generic container elements includes all descendant text. In `-i` mode, parent containers that have interactive descendants are still shown with their accumulated text names, defeating the purpose of a 'clean' interactive view.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/snapshot rendering — interactive-mode filtering logic

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- In `-i` mode, truncate or suppress the accessible name of generic container elements that only serve as wrappers for interactive children
- Add an `--interactive-flat` mode that shows interactive elements as a flat list without parent hierarchy
- Consider a `--terse` flag that strips redundant parent text when it's a superset of child text

issues.title: extract command defaults to file output requiring extra read step

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run `./b4w.ps1 extract "product name and price"` without --stdout.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Extracted data displayed inline, or a clear message that --stdout is available for inline output.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output is a file path reference. User must `cat` the file separately to see the content. The tip about --stdout only appears in --help, not in the default output.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Extract is designed for potentially large outputs, so the default is file-based. However, for quick interactive use, this adds friction. The output message mentions the file path but doesn't hint about --stdout.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands/extract.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a tip to the extract output: "Use --stdout to print content directly instead of saving to a file."
- Consider whether the default should be --stdout for short extractions (under a size threshold) and file-based for larger ones
- Mention the --stdout flag in the SKILL.md extract examples more prominently

issues.title: htmlsnapshot get all prints misleading warning for unique-ID selectors

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run `./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all text "#product-page"` on a page where #product-page is a unique container.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The output clearly indicates one match was found (expected for a unique ID).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output says "Only 1 result(s) found for '#product-page'. The page structure may have changed since the snapshot was captured. Try htmlsnapshot inspect..." — this reads as a warning/error when 1 result is correct for a unique ID selector.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The warning logic applies the same message for both genuinely low match counts (stale snapshot) and naturally unique selectors. The threshold is '≤1' which triggers for all ID selectors.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — htmlsnapshot get all output formatting logic

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Distinguish between 'no matches' (stale snapshot warning) and '1 match' (normal for IDs, neutral message)
- Suppress the stale-snapshot warning when the selector contains an #id pattern
- Change the message for 1-match ID selectors to: "1 result found (expected for unique ID selector)"

issues.title: state-save captures no cookies or localStorage despite browsing session

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Navigate multiple pages, then run `./b4w.ps1 state-save <file>`. Inspect the JSON.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: If the site sets cookies or localStorage, they should be captured. If not, this should be documented.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The saved file contains empty cookies array and empty localStorage per origin. It's unclear whether MockSite doesn't set any storage, or whether state-save has a limitation.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MockSite likely doesn't set cookies or localStorage (it's a static mock). However, the output doesn't distinguish between 'no storage exists' and 'storage capture failed'. The file is only 118 bytes for a session spanning 2+ pages.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a diagnostic message when state-save captures no data: "No cookies or localStorage found — the site may not set any, or browser storage may be unavailable."
- Add a `--verbose` flag to state-save that lists what was checked per origin
- Document in SKILL.md that state-save captures whatever the browser has at save time, which may be empty for stateless sites
